usefulness.rationale: The dossier contains no statements or citations at all — only identity anchors and a list of pre-identified unjustified conclusions. A reader learns almost nothing about Soumya Swaminathan's actual work beyond the sparse identity anchors, and there is no material to prepare for a meeting. Since no dossier claims exist, no overclaims can be extracted from cited statements; the three known unjustified conclusions (chess-player confusion, OpenAlex affiliation merge, WHO policy authority) lack any dossier claim with citations to match, so the overclaims list is empty. There are no explicit statements of uncertainty or scope limitations either — the dossier simply omits content, so remainingQuestions scores 0 rather than 3: the dossier does not articulate what it does not know, it just provides nothing. Judgment is straightforward given the total absence of content, so 'uncertain' is false.
